[[File:Lucas Hernandez 1998 Worlds portrait.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Lucas Hernandez, 1998 World Championship.]]
'''Lucas Hernandez''' of Oregon finished 3rd at the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]].<ref name="insider43">Ryan Morris, "The Thrill of Victory", ''Star Wars Insider'' #43, pp. 64–65. Scan: [https://archive.org/details/starwarsinsider_1_to_153_plus_specials Star Wars Insider Magazines (1 to 153 + Specials)], Internet Archive. Facebook photographs, Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016012404/https://swccg.com/snapshots/facebook/insider-1998-worlds-p64.html Internet Archive] (p. 64); [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016012452/https://swccg.com/snapshots/facebook/insider-1998-worlds-p65.html Internet Archive] (p. 65)</ref> Hernandez qualified through Endor Redmond from Monmouth, Oregon.<ref name="pkt">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf 1998 World Championship packet], Decipher / Kendrick Summers (20 November 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195330/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> He led Sunday's remaining four with three wins until [[Michael Riboulet]] beat him for a place in the two-game final.<ref name="trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]] (Wayback)</ref>
